newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb blast near Kashmir leader's home kills one.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast near Kashmir leader's home kills one.

text.p: One person was killed and six wounded when a powerful bomb exploded near the home of the chief minister of India's Jammu and Kashmir state on Friday, Indian police said.
Chief minister Farooq Abdullah was not in the Kashmir Valley at the time, they said.

Jamait-ul-Mujahideen, a hardline militant group, claimed responsibility for the blast which went off about 30 metres (yards) from Abdullah's residence on Gupkar Road in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
A Jamait-ul-Mujahideen spokesman who called local news organisations to claim responsibility said attacks would continue on pro-India leaders in the troubled state.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in Kashmir since a separatist revolt erupted in 1990.
Police said the land mine went off near a small tea stall on Gupkar Road, a high-security area where at least four members of Abdullah's cabinet live.
Abdullah, whose pro-India National Conference party swept state elections in September, escaped several attempts on his life during the campaign.
On Wednesday, a junior minister in Abdullah's government escaped an attack by separatist guerrillas while he was paying his respects to his deceased father in a cemetery in Srinagar.
The militants threw two grenades which exploded about 50 metres (yards) from junior Home (Interior) Minister Mohmood Ahmad Sagar. One policeman was injured in Wednesday's attack.
